key_insight: Adding differential privacy to federated learning degrades the clarity and fidelity of model explanations; this paper quantifies that trade-off and provides practical guidance to balance privacy and interpretability.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap in understanding how Differential Privacy (DP) applied in Federated Learning (FL) affects explainability (XAI) of models and what adjustments practitioners can make to preserve interpretable outputs while maintaining privacy.
method: Systematic evaluation of FL models trained with varying DP privacy budgets to measure changes in explainability.
Apply feature-attribution XAI methods (e.g., SHAP/LIME-style analyses) and concrete explainability metrics (fidelity, sparsity, stability) to compare private vs. non-private models.
Analyze trade-offs and derive practical recommendations (e.g., budget tuning, model simplification, feature selection) to mitigate explainability loss under DP.
impact: Gives ML practitioners actionable insight on how privacy mechanisms affect interpretability, enabling informed choices of DP settings and model design to retain useful explanations in privacy-preserving FL deployments.
visual_elements: Trade-off curve: privacy budget (ε) on x-axis vs. explainability metric (fidelity/stability) on y-axis showing degradation as privacy increases.
Pipeline diagram: FL clients → local training + DP noise → secure aggregator → global model → XAI module producing explanations.
Bar/heatmap comparison: explainability metrics across multiple privacy budgets and model architectures (with/without feature selection).
Checklist/decision flow: recommended mitigation steps (tune ε, simplify model, reduce features) to recover explainability under DP.
paper_title: Towards Explainable Federated Learning: Understanding the Impact of Differential Privacy
paper_authors: Júlio Oliveira, Rodrigo Ferreira, André Riker, Glaucio H. S. Carvalho, Eirini Eleni Tsilopoulou
